{{Quote|Agh!|Guard shouting as he was killed by Starkiller|<ref name="TFU">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref>}}
This '''Shadow Guard''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who was part of the [[Emperor's Shadow Guard]], and was stationed on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]. He was [[Death/Legends|killed]] when [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] apprentice, [[Galen Marek]], arrived on the planet in search of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]].

==Biography==
At some point, he became an [[Emperor's Shadow Guard]], elite guardsmen of the [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Emperor's Royal Guard]]. In [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], when [[Galen Marek]], secret apprentice of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], [[Mission to Nar Shaddaa (Galen Marek)|visited]] the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] to find [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]], the guardsman was sent with a task force to [[Death/Legends|kill]] him. The apprentice got past all of his [[Imperial Navy commando]]s, and then engaged the guard in duel at the front of [[The Undertow]], a bar that Kota was at, with the latter ambushing him with a [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Push|Force Push]], and first sent a wave of EVO Troopers to take on Marek. After a while, the guardsman summoned his [[Shadow stormtrooper/Legends|Shadow Troopers]] to aid him. Even so, he was still overpowered by the apprentice; who used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to repel him out of the bar as the latter attempted to use a Force Grip on his foe, killing him.

==Skills & abilities==
As a Shadow Guard, he was proficient with a [[Lightsaber pike/Legends|lightsaber pike]], using it in the duel. The guardsmen also was able to use the Force to some extent, producing [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]] and able to [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Choke|Force choke]]. In the end, his skills were no match for that of Marek's.

==Behind the scenes==
This Shadow Guard appears only in the Wii and PS2 versions for ''The Force Unleashed'', largely because of Cloud City being replaced with Nar Shaddaa in those versions.
